key_claims_and_derivations.claim: Mean lifetime tau is 1/lambda_tot; half-life T_1/2 = tau ln 2; resonance energy width Gamma_tot = hbar * lambda_tot. If given Gamma_tot, it must first be divided by hbar before entering rate equations. In rate formulas where the dimensioned constant already incorporates hbar and permittivity, neither hbar nor ln 2 may be multiplied again. Directional misidentification leads to factor 1/ln2 (~1.443, +44.3%) or ln2 (~0.693, -30.7%).
key_claims_and_derivations.locator: Suhonen 2007, printed p. 118, Eq. (6.1); thesis Section 5.9.1

key_claims_and_derivations.claim: Total transition rate is lambda_k = lambda_gamma,k * (1 + alpha_k), where alpha_k is total internal conversion coefficient. Total branching ratio b_k = lambda_k / lambda_tot yields lambda_gamma,k = b_k / [tau * (1 + alpha_k)]. Partial photon branching ratio b_gamma,k = lambda_gamma,k / lambda_tot satisfies sum b_gamma <= 1 (strictly < 1 with IC). Observed photon fraction r_k = a_k / sum a_j does not equal b_k or b_gamma,k. Normalization using relative photon intensities a_k requires complete decay channels with zero unobserved E0 conversion or particle emission.

Real multipole mixing ratio delta(E2/M1) is the ratio of photon emission probability amplitudes, governed by triangular condition |Ii-If| <= L <= Ii+If and parity conservation. Photon fractions are delta²/(1+delta²) for E2 and 1/(1+delta²) for M1. The effective ICC alpha_mix must be weighted by the same photon fractions. RME relation requires consistent SI/Gaussian magnetic operator definition. Phase convention changes do not alter physical quantities delta² or partial rates.
key_claims_and_derivations.locator: Lange, Kumar & Hamilton 1982, printed pp. 121–122, Eqs. (2.1)–(2.6); thesis Section 5.9.3

key_claims_and_derivations.claim: Downwards B(XL; i->f) = |<f||M(XL)||i>|² / (2Ii+1); reciprocal relation (2Ii+1)B(i->f) = (2If+1)B(f->i). Reconstructed textbook constants from Suhonen printed numbers: C_E2 = 1.2250333078e9 s^-1 MeV^-5 (e² fm⁴)^-1, C_M1 = 1.7583758801e13 s^-1 MeV^-3 [(mu_N/c)²]^-1.
key_claims_and_derivations.locator: Suhonen 2007, printed pp. 118–120, Eqs. (6.3), (6.4), (6.12)–(6.14); thesis Section 5.9.4

key_claims_and_derivations.claim: In branching ratios from the same parent state, the mean lifetime tau algebraically cancels out. However, mixing ratio uncertainties, ICC model errors, detector efficiency curve slopes, and peak area covariances (positive or negative) remain. Across different parent states, lifetime and stopping-power uncertainties do not automatically cancel unless sensitivities match. Profile likelihood multimodality must not be conflated with posterior distribution (which requires explicit prior).

Görgen et al. (2004) DSAM measurement in 163Lu provided valuable new lifetimes, but interband absolute B(E2) and B(M1) strengths adopted thin-target branching ratios (Jensen 2002) and low-spin average mixing ratio delta = -3.10. Similar Qt was used by authors within their specific wobbling picture, but Table I Qt values show broad variation and the ~4% difference was their specific model estimate. Observed transition properties do not exclude quasiparticle-alignment or gamma-soft competing mechanisms.
key_claims_and_derivations.locator: Görgen et al. 2004, PDF pp. 2–4, Tables I–II; thesis Section 5.9.7

channel_1.multipolarity: M1 + E2 (permitted by |4-3| <= L <= 4+3 and parity; both assumed contributing in teaching model)

channel_2.multipolarity: predominantly E2 (L=1 forbidden by |4-2| <= L <= 4+2; higher multipoles M3/E4 assumed negligible)

boundaries_and_transition.transition_scope: Section 5.9 establishes the empirical rate-to-B(XL) causal chain. The B(XL) values provide squared moduli of matrix elements and serve as direct inputs for statistical inference in Section 5.10 and microscopic/collective dynamic model comparisons in Chapter 4.
boundaries_and_transition.unresolved_empirical_inputs: Precise branchings when unobserved E0 or particle emission channels compete; experimental detector response waveforms outside scope of current section; stopping power model systematic errors in DSAM.
